Series::traverse_put¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::traverse_put(pluss::RangeView<ExtractSpec> specs, const Series& values) const -> Series

What It Does¶

Returns a patched copy after writing through a selector that must remain view-representable.

This is the value-semantic sibling of traverse_put_(). The write rules are the same, the accepted selector subset is the same, and the selector normalization is the same. The difference is ownership:

  • traverse_put_() mutates the current Series

  • traverse_put() leaves the current Series alone and returns a modified copy

So traverse_put() is the method to choose when you want a clean “derive a patched result” style, but you also want the selector itself constrained to plain traversal and view semantics.

Parameters¶

specs (pluss::RangeView<ExtractSpec>)

The destination selector.

This method accepts only the view-representable subset shared with traverse_slice() and traverse_put_():

  • scalar indices

  • positive-step slices

  • SliceAll()

  • Ellipsis()

  • NewAxis()

Rejected selectors include:

  • negative-step slices

  • bool masks

  • integer index Series

  • any mixed selector that requires materialized advanced indexing

NewAxis() is allowed because it is only result-shape bookkeeping; it does not turn the write into advanced indexing.

values (const Series&)

The replacement data.

Two value modes are supported:

  • scalar source: broadcast across the selected destination region

  • non-scalar source: element count must exactly match the selected destination element count

The selector gate is stricter than extract_put(), but the write-cardinality rules are the same once the selector has been accepted.

Returns¶

Series A new Series containing the write result.

Examples¶

Example 1. Shared setup. This starting grid matches the state produced by the verified in-place examples.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, 100.0, 12.0, 13.5},
    {2.0, 200.0, 22.0, 23.5},
    {3.0, 300.0, -5.0, 33.5},
});

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 100, 12, 13.5],
  [2, 200, 22, 23.5],
  [3, 300, -5, 33.5]]

Example 2. A copy-returning write patches the result and leaves the source unchanged.

auto copied = grid.traverse_put(
    {std::int64_t{0}, pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(0, 2, 1)},
    pluss::make_series(999.0));

std::cout << copied;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[999, 999, 12, 13.5],
  [2, 200, 22, 23.5],
  [3, 300, -5, 33.5]]

Example 3. The original input is still unchanged after traverse_put().

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 100, 12, 13.5],
  [2, 200, 22, 23.5],
  [3, 300, -5, 33.5]]

Example 4. NewAxis() is still legal on the copy-returning surface.

std::cout << grid.traverse_put(
                 {pluss::Slicing::NewAxis(), pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(), std::int64_t{0}},
                 pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0}));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, 100, 12, 13.5],
  [20, 200, 22, 23.5],
  [30, 300, -5, 33.5]]

The added axis affects selector normalization, not the final writable rank.

Example 5. Ellipsis() is part of the accepted view-representable subset here too.

std::cout << grid.traverse_put(
                 {pluss::Slicing::Ellipsis(), std::int64_t{2}},
                 pluss::make_series({120.0, 220.0, 320.0}));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 100, 120, 13.5],
  [2, 200, 220, 23.5],
  [3, 300, 320, 33.5]]

Example 6. Reverse slices are rejected because they are not view-representable on this surface.

try {
  std::cout << grid.traverse_put(
                   {pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(), pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(-1, pluss::Slicing::Slice::kUnbounded, -1)},
                   pluss::make_series(0.0));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::traverse_put: selector is not view-representable; use extract() or extract_put() for materializing paths

Example 7. Bool masks are rejected for the same reason.

try {
  auto row_mask = pluss::make_series({true, false, true});
  std::cout << grid.traverse_put(
                   {row_mask, pluss::Slicing::SliceAll()},
                   pluss::make_series(0.0));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::traverse_put: selector is not view-representable; use extract() or extract_put() for materializing paths

Example 8. Cardinality mismatches still fail after selector admission, and that message comes from the shared selector-write machinery.

try {
  std::cout << grid.traverse_put(
                   {std::int64_t{0}, pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(0, 2, 1)},
                   pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::extract_put: source must be scalar or match selected element count

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • traverse_put() is strict by design. It rejects selectors that would require materialized advanced indexing.

  • NewAxis() is accepted, but it is only selector bookkeeping.

  • Reverse slices, masks, and integer index Series are all rejected here even though extract_put() can accept them.

  • Some later validation errors mention extract_put because both methods share the same downstream write-cardinality checks after the selector has been accepted.

Summary¶

Use traverse_put() when you want value semantics and a selector gate that stays inside ordinary traversal and view rules. If your selector needs masked or materialized addressing, move to extract_put(). If the selector is still strict-view-friendly but you want mutation, move to traverse_put_().
